circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern addition to the F1 calendar, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit winds around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support categories and racing events. As an FIA Grade 1 certified street circuit, it serves as a premier motorsport venue in Australia.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Red Bull Ring near Spielberg in Austria is a 4. 326 km circuit that previously operated under different names while hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate periods: initially as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then following renovation and reconfiguration as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix before being renamed the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first-ever Formula One grand prix held in the Middle East that same year. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various motorsport events including GP2 racing, drag racing, Australian V8 Supercars (2006-2010), and 24-hour endurance competitions, and operates with FIA Grade 1 certification across multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One teams. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Ardennes region of Belgium, Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km circuit that has served as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925, making it one of Formula One's most historic venues. The track has featured on the championship calendar continuously from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, and was present at the sport's inaugural season in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in the sport's premier series, the track has accommodated various international racing competitions including sports car championships and North American racing series throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in China's Jiading district served as the traditional home of the Chinese Grand Prix, hosting the prestigious race from 2004 until 2019 before resuming in 2024. Beyond Formula One, the venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing competitions beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located in Northamptonshire, England, is the traditional home of the British Grand Prix, having hosted the race since 1948 and serving as the venue for the inaugural 1950 World Championship race. After rotating with two other circuits between 1955 and 1986, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, and the track continues to host international motorsport events including MotoGP races.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit near Budapest, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city following government preference over an original plan for a street circuit through Budapest's largest park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track established in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. The venue hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, making it one of just four circuits to maintain continuous Formula One calendar presence since the championship's inception, and earned its nickname "Temple of Speed" for its notably fast straights and high-speed layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda's subsidiary, hosting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is most renowned for staging rounds of the Formula One World Championship and Japanese Super Formula series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track threading through Paradise, Nevada that incorporates the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The 3. 8-mile layout showcases the region's iconic hospitality venues and architectural landmarks, creating a unique racing environment through the heart of the casino district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's 4. 3-kilometre Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two brothers, Ricardo and Pedro, who both perished in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned to Formula One's calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, hosting the Mexican Grand Prix on a revised configuration distinct from its previous layouts used between earlier decades.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners designed specifically for Formula One racing. Hosting the Miami Grand Prix since 2022, the track achieves average qualifying speeds of approximately 139 mph and has recently accommodated Formula E competition with a modified configuration beginning in the 2025-26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling Monaco's harbor within the principality. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known by the Monte Carlo designation, reflecting its predominant location within that neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 to 2026 before departing the Formula One calendar. The track earned its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname from its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz, which create a distinctive undulating racing experience through the North Sea dunes.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail. Spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track includes a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront. Since its inaugural year in 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and from 2025 onwards also hosts international electric motorsport racing.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a track that traces the perimeter of Marina Bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the 4. 657 km Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP and the FIA World Endurance Championship, while previously accommodating various other racing series from IndyCar to sports car competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand as his racing nationality.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One world title with Mercedes in 2026, setting the record as the sport's youngest champion, having claimed nine race victories since joining the grid in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes in the sport's premier racing championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing the Audi team in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has secured two runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during his time at Mercedes, achieving this feat in consecutive years 2019 and 2020. Currently competing for Cadillac, Bottas has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13-season career in Formula One.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Alpine team. He brings South American representation to the sport's premier racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian endurance racing driver currently competing in LMP2 for AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series. He holds a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One, where he has started seven races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has secured seven World Drivers' Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple circuit records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved notable success in endurance racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 world championship standings. Throughout his nine seasons in Formula One, he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish driver who previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the FIA World Endurance Championship, driving for WRT as a factory driver with BMW.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship after eight seasons in the sport. He has accumulated 14 Grand Prix victories during his time in the championship.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, most recently drove for Haas in Formula One. He achieved his sole grand prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while representing Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, currently races for McLaren in Formula One and has claimed nine race victories during his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One spanning 2011 to 2024, accumulating eight race victories throughout his 14-year career in the sport. Known by his "Honey Badger" moniker, he established himself as a consistent competitor across more than a decade of top-level motorsport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the championship.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship, where he will drive for Ford after previously racing in the LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda enjoyed a full-time Formula One career spanning 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 Formula One seasons, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China's sole contribution to Formula One's driver roster, having competed in the championship from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, adopting the name of Renault's sports car division while maintaining its identity as the manufacturer's factory entry. Originally operating as Renault F1 Team under Groupe Renault's ownership, Alpine represented Renault's works programme until the automotive group's withdrawal from the championship following the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has entered Formula One competition through different organizational structures, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, is Formula One's longest-standing and most accomplished outfit, participating in every championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially dubbed "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, remains the most decorated entity in the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas commenced racing in 2016, establishing itself as a newer entrant to the grid. The team, currently led by principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, has operated since its 2014 establishment through the present day.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering outfit established itself in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993, where it competed as an independent constructor for over three decades. The team achieved legendary status in sportscar competition, including overall victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours, before departing Formula One in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving teams by race count. Audi acquired the operation in 2024 to serve as the technical and competitive foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship. The team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. The Mercedes-AMG Petronas outfit achieved a significant restructuring in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff in a tri-partite ownership arrangement. The marque's racing identity carries the storied "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as a sister outfit within the Red Bull F1 operation.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as a second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with facilities near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as part of Red Bull's dual-team structure in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licenced Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH since its 2005 establishment. Led by Christian Horner through 2024, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025, while remaining part of Red Bull's two-team racing portfolio alongside Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and remains one of the sport's longest-established independent constructors.
